newsitem.title: HONDURAS: Two dead, 10 wounded in Honduras protests.
newsitem.headline: Two dead, 10 wounded in Honduras protests.

text.p: Two people died and 10 others were injured as protesters clashed with police and the army in eastern Honduras on Wednesday, officials said.

Police and army troops forcibly dislodged some 1,000 residents of El Paraiso, some 80 miles (110 km) east of the capital Tegucigalpa, after they had occupied a section of the Pan-American highway on Tuesday to protest the highway's poor condition.
Wilmer Figueroa, 16, and Cristino Diaz, whose age was not available, were killed during the incident, although officials did not say how they died.
"In the fighting there were two people killed and another dozen police officers and soldiers injured," said Col. Neptali Lara, head of the army in the district, told Reuters.
Honduran President Carlos Roberto Reina blamed the protesters for the violence and said security forces had acted to "guarantee the interests of the public at large."
But the government's National Commission for Human Rights director Leo Valladares told Reuters police forces acted irresponsibly.
"The way this protest was put down was exaggerated, abusive," he said.
